senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; קָוָה)gathering of water, esp. the ritual bath of purification.
units: Yoma VIII, 9 (play on מקוה hope, Jer. XVII, 13) מה מ׳ מטהר וכ׳ as the bath purifies the unclean, so does the Lord &c. Ib. 31ᵃ מי מ׳ ארבעים סאה the contents of a ritual bath must be forty S’ah; Num. R. s. 18.
Mikv. I, 7 שוה למ׳ וכ׳ has the qualification of a ritual miḳveh when gathered in a pond, contrad. to מַעְיָן; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. means of purification.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 64a:5">Kidd. 64ᵃ</cite> <he>בנות ישראל מִקְוֵה טהרה וכ׳</he> daughters of common Israelites are the means of purity (reinstatement to priestly status) for (the issue of) degraded priests, i.e. the daughter of an Israelite woman and a degraded priest may marry into priesthood; <cite ref="Kiddushin 77a:8">ib. 77ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Kiddushin 5:3">Tosef. ib. V, 3</cite>; a. e.—Pl. <he>מִקְווֹת</he>, <he>מִקְוָאוֹת</he>, <he>מִקְוָו׳</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 4:8:4">Y. Ter. IV, 43ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>שני מקוות</he>; <cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 2:3">Mikv. II, 3</cite> <he>שני מ׳ וכ׳</he> two adjacent reservoirs one of which contains &c.
Ib. I, 1; a. fr.—Miḳvaoth, name of a treatise of Mishnah and Tosefta of the Order of Tohăroth.
